text: Waited forty minutes at the counter for my blood pressure pills and they still had the wrong dose ready. Back again Thursday.
Rent went out this morning and the account is down to $212 until the 15th. Ramen week.
The grey cat from number 9 sat on our fence for two solid hours, watching a single sparrow. Neither of them moved. I respect the commitment.
Finally finished the left sleeve. Only about six more rows of ribbing on the right one and the cardigan is done.
Dropped Maya at the airport at 5:40am. House is far too quiet and I keep checking my phone for her landing time.
Missed the 7:12 train by about ten seconds. Watched it pull out while I stood there holding a very hot coffee.
Dad called. He sounded tired but laughed at my joke about the lawn mower, so that's something.
Third night in a row I've woken at 3am with my heart racing for no reason. Not telling anyone yet.
Found a perfect little river stone near the bridge, flat and grey with a white stripe. It's on my desk now.
Boss said 'let's circle back' about my raise. I know what that means.

Spent the evening at the community centre helping Mrs. Okafor learn to video call her grandson in Leeds. It took three tries and a lot of pointing at the screen. When his face finally popped up she clapped her hands like a kid. I stayed for tea afterwards and she gave me a jar of her pepper sauce to take home.

Replaced the washer in the kitchen tap this afternoon. The hardware store guy on Delancey Road sold me the wrong size first, so it was two trips. Tap doesn't drip now though, and the whole thing cost $3.40. Felt oddly proud.

Priya got a B-minus on her chemistry quiz and went straight to her room without saying anything. I made her favourite noodles and left a bowl outside the door. Twenty minutes later the bowl was empty and she came down and sat next to me on the sofa. We watched a baking show and didn't talk about it. That seemed right.

Quoted a bathroom retile for the Hendersons today. Eleven hundred for labour, they want the herringbone pattern, which means extra cuts and extra swearing. I think they'll say yes. Need to order 14 boxes of the matte white ones by Friday or the supplier won't have them until November.

Lecture on organic reactions at 9 and I understood about half of it. Sat with Tomasz in the library afterwards and we went through the mechanisms on a whiteboard until the cleaner kicked us out. Exam is in nine days. I should probably stop checking my phone every four minutes.

The new neighbours have a drum kit. A real one. It started at 4pm and went on until nearly six. I'm not even that annoyed because the kid is actually getting better at the fill in the middle of that one song.

Walked the whole Cliff Path loop with Ruth, nearly eight miles. Wind was brutal on the headland but the sea was this strange milky green. We ate cheese sandwiches on a bench and a gull tried to take mine. My knees are going to remind me of this tomorrow.

Sorted through all the receipts for the tax return at the kitchen table. Turns out I paid for the same software subscription twice last year, which is $118 I'll never see again. Put everything into one folder and labelled it properly for once. Accountant appointment is the 22nd.

The sourdough finally rose properly. Fed the starter twice a day for nine days and kept it by the radiator. Crust crackled on the cooling rack, which my grandmother always said meant good luck. Gave half the loaf to the lady downstairs.

Had a long call with my sister about who is driving Mum to her hip appointment on the 14th. We both have work. She offered to take the morning, I'll do the afternoon pickup. Mum insists she can take a bus. She cannot take a bus.

Client paid invoice 0043 nineteen days late, no apology. I've started adding a late fee line to every quote. Also redrew the logo for the bakery job three times and they picked the very first version. Freelancing in a nutshell.

Bought a used road bike off a guy in Carlow for 240 euro. It needs new brake pads and the saddle is hideous, but the frame is solid. Rode it up and down the estate road until the streetlights came on. Grinning like an idiot the whole time.
I walked past the old school today and the climbing frame is gone. Just a square of bark chips. Stood at the railing a lot longer than a grown man should. I could still hear the clang of the bell.

Had my shift swapped without anyone telling me, so I turned up at six to find the kitchen dark. Rang Dev, who said sorry about forty times. Went home, made eggs on toast, and fell asleep on the sofa by eight. Honestly, not the worst accident.

The dentist said I need a crown on the back molar. Nine hundred and fifty pounds, maybe a bit less with the plan. I nodded calmly and then sat in the car park for ten minutes doing sums on the back of the appointment card.
Haven't painted in six weeks. Today I squeezed out the blues and just sat looking at them. Eventually did a small study of the kettle. It's bad, but my hands remembered what to do.

Told Gus we can't afford the trip to the coast this year. He took it better than I did. We're going to the lake with the tent instead, and he's already planning a fishing schedule on the back of a cereal box.

Spent an hour on hold with the broadband company only to be told the technician visit is next Wednesday between 8 and 6. Eight to six! Like I have nothing else to do. Working from the library until it's sorted.

Marching band rehearsal ran long again. Mr. Fenwick made us do the same sixteen bars of the closing piece until the trombones stopped rushing. My lip is swollen and I'm starving but we sounded great at the end. Football game on Friday.
My hands shook when I opened the letter. Not bad news, thank goodness, just the results from the scan being normal. I cried in the hallway anyway and then ate half a packet of biscuits.

The garden is finally giving something back. Pulled up eleven carrots, two of them forked like little legs, and picked a bowl of runner beans. Pete from the allotment next door says the tomatoes will go blotchy if I don't pinch out the side shoots. Noted.

Trying to decide between the two flats. The one on Birch Street is cheaper by $90 a month but there's a bus depot behind it. The other has a balcony and a landlord who answered my email within an hour. I think my gut has already chosen.

Sat in on my daughter's recital. She played the Clementi sonatina with only one wobble, and then looked straight at me with this tiny, determined smile. I'd forgotten how nervous I get on her behalf. Took her for hot chocolate afterwards and she critiqued every note.

Forklift on bay 4 clipped a pallet today, nobody hurt, but the whole warehouse went quiet for a minute. We had a safety huddle at the end of the shift and the supervisor actually listened. I'm picking up overtime on Saturday if my back holds out.

Found out the other side of the street are all getting solar panels. Quote for ours came back at 7,400 with a payback of eleven years. I'd be 73 by then. Still, the numbers are not crazy. Will ask Linda what she thinks.

Started the day all wrong. Alarm didn't go off because the phone died overnight, so I woke at ten past eight instead of six forty and had nineteen minutes to get the kids dressed and fed. Oscar refused to wear anything but the dinosaur jumper, which is in the wash, so we compromised on the green one with the hole in the elbow. Dropped them at school with seconds to spare and got a look from the head teacher at the gate. At work Carla from accounts wanted the quarterly spreadsheet and I hadn't touched it. I told her Thursday and then stayed until seven on Tuesday. Not my finest hour. Walking home I passed the florist and bought a bunch of cheap tulips for no reason, yellow ones. The house smelled like burnt toast when I opened the door because my husband had tried to make dinner, bless him. We ate cereal on the sofa and watched the one about the penguins. Lily asked why penguins don't get cold feet. I had no answer. I think I might ring Mum this weekend, I owe her a call, and she'll want the full report on the school gate look.

Retirement is not the empty field I feared. Mornings now are the radio, two slices of toast and the crossword, which I do in pen because I'm vain. Last Tuesday Harold and I took the 38 bus out to the reservoir and walked round it, three and a half miles, slow but steady. His wife passed in the spring and he still hasn't told his son how bad the evenings are. I told him mine are just as long and we both laughed too hard at that. The pension came through at the new rate, which is about forty pounds less than they estimated, so I've cancelled the newspaper and the gym I never went to. I'm thinking of volunteering at the library on Wednesdays, shelving. Janice there says they need someone with decent knees and steady hands. The boiler made a clunking sound again too. I'll have to find a plumber who isn't a cousin of somebody. Also the cat is limping, so vet on Friday, possibly. Overall a decent week, if I'm honest. Better than I would have guessed a year ago.

Spent most of the afternoon at the clinic with my son's cast. They took the plaster off and his arm looks so thin and pale, like something that lived under a rock. The doctor said another three weeks of no football, which Jamie took like a prison sentence. Waited in a corridor with a vending machine that kept eating coins. Then to the supermarket for the weekly shop, which was a mistake on a Saturday. The queue at the checkout stretched to the cereal aisle. I forgot the bin bags and the lemons, of course. Home by four, and the kids were already fighting over the controller. My neighbour Dolores dropped round a tray of enchiladas because she saw the cast earlier in the week and wanted to help, which nearly made me cry on the doorstep. Fed everyone, did the dishes, put on a wash, and then sat on the back step for ten minutes in the dusk. A plane went over, low and slow. I haven't been anywhere since March and every plane makes me restless. Maybe next spring we really will go to Lisbon like I keep saying.

Monday. The van wouldn't start in the cold, so I lost an hour waiting for the neighbour's jump leads. Got to the Patel job late, apologised, and was forgiven because I'd brought a box of samosas from that place on Kent Road. The wall they wanted opened up turned out to have a gas pipe behind it that wasn't on any plan, so we stopped and called the gas fitter. I hate that feeling, knowing a day's pay just evaporated. Used the downtime to measure the loft instead, which they'd asked about, and quoted that for another eighteen hundred. Afterwards I picked up my daughter from swim practice, and she told me the whole saga of her friend and a stolen goggles incident in great detail while I tried to listen and also not miss the turn. At home the invoice drawer was a disaster, so I sorted everything into three piles: paid, owed, ignored. The ignored pile is bigger than I'd like. Sam called about the football on Sunday, I said yes, I'll bring crisps. My shoulder is aching again from the drilling. Need to book that physio before it turns into something worse.

We finally did the thing we'd put off for two years and went to see the lake house where Gran grew up. Four hours in the car with the radio on low, Mum navigating from a map that is older than I am. The house is mostly gone, to be honest. There's a boarded porch and a young maple growing through the old kitchen floor. But the lake was still the same slate colour and the air smelled of pine and cold water. Mum stood at the edge for a long time and then told me about the winter the lake froze so solidly that the whole village skated across to the church. She'd never mentioned it before. We had lunch at a diner nearby, the kind with laminated menus and pie behind glass, and I had a slice of rhubarb that was better than it had any right to be. On the way home Mum fell asleep somewhere past the quarry and I drove the last stretch in silence, thinking about how little I know about her childhood. I should record her. Tomorrow I'll buy a notebook. Also need petrol, the light came on near the junction and I ignored it.

Our team lost the quarter-final 2-1 on a penalty in the ninetieth minute and I have not really recovered. Spent most of the evening on the pitch trying not to look at anyone. Coach Reilly said something decent about heads up and next season, which I mostly didn't hear. Got home to find a cold plate of pasta in the fridge from my mother with a note that said eat this, you've got a face like a wet weekend. She isn't wrong. After the shower I scrolled through photos from the first match of the season, when we were all so cheerful and awful, and got a bit sentimental. Marcus texted a thumbs up and a sad face. My calf is tight, there's a bruise on my shin the size of a plum. Maths homework is due tomorrow and I haven't started, so I'm going to do it now, quickly, while ignoring all the better things I could be doing, like sleeping. The rain has started up outside and it's drumming on the shed roof, which is a nice noise. Maybe things look better once it's light.

I think I've decided to leave the agency. It took me about fourteen months and a stack of Sunday-night stomach aches to admit it. Today they handed me yet another account that nobody wanted, with a deadline for next Wednesday and a budget of nothing, and I smiled and said sure. Walking out to the car park I felt it, very clearly, that sinking in the chest that has nothing to do with being busy. So tonight I did the numbers. If I go freelance I need about 3,200 a month to break even, and I have six months of savings and two clients who'd probably follow me. Ana says I should do it. My dad says think about the pension. Both are right. I made a list of the things I'd miss: the Friday lunches, the good coffee machine, Mohammed from design. A shorter list than I expected. Then I wrote out a draft email to my manager, and didn't send it. Tomorrow I'll look at the draft again over breakfast. Also need to tell the landlord about the leaking window, it's been three weeks, and buy a birthday card for Ana's mum.

A very ordinary Sunday that I liked more than I expected. Slept until nine, which I haven't done since I had the baby. Made pancakes with Theo standing on the step stool, flour everywhere, one pancake in the shape of a lopsided heart. Then my wife took him to the park and I had the house to myself for the first time in what felt like weeks. I put on the old records, the ones I'd packed away, and did nothing in particular. Vacuumed the spare room, swapped the sheets, fixed the loose hinge on the bathroom cabinet. It's amazing what you can do when no one is climbing you. In the afternoon we all went round to my brother's for roast chicken, and his new girlfriend Anneka turned out to be properly funny. She and Theo had a very serious conversation about trucks. The drive home was quiet, Theo snoring in the back with a stolen bread roll in his fist. Bills are due Tuesday: electricity 143, car insurance 61. I'll do it first thing. Back to work Monday and I find I don't mind.

Weird day, mostly in a good way. I took the early bus to the big market in the old part of town to buy fabric for the curtains. The stalls open at seven and by half past the best bolts are gone, so you have to be quick and slightly ruthless. I got four metres of a heavy mustard linen for eleven pounds a metre, plus a card of brass hooks that I probably don't need. Chatted with the man at the next stall who sells only buttons. Only buttons! He has a drawer system that would make a librarian weep. Then coffee, then home, then three hours cutting and pinning with the radio on. The first curtain hangs crooked but I can fix it. My sister rang while I had a mouthful of pins and I couldn't answer, so now she's convinced something is wrong. I'll ring back. Tomorrow I need to find the receipt for the washing machine, it's making a noise like a goat, and the warranty is up in August. I might take a photo of the receipt and the serial number so I never hunt for it again. Probably won't.

Slow day at the allotment. The leeks are fat, the squash has gone mad, and some creature has been at the lettuces again. I think it's a rabbit but Pete swears it's a fox. Sat in the shed with a flask of tea and watched the rain run down the little window. There's something about a wet shed on a grey afternoon that settles the mind. I thought about Bill, who had this plot before me, and who left a biscuit tin of seeds with labels in handwriting I can hardly read. Some of the labels say things like 'good red one' and 'from Doreen'. I planted a row of those this spring and I still don't know what they are. Might be beans. On the way home I stopped for fish and chips and ate them on the wall by the church, in the drizzle, like a teenager. The chip shop man asked after my knee, which I hadn't realised he'd noticed. At home the answering machine blinked, my niece, wanting to know if she can borrow the ladder. Of course she can. I'll fix the wobbly rung first. Early night, I think.

Interview day. Woke up at five with my stomach in knots, ironed the blue shirt twice, and rehearsed the answer to 'tell us about a time you failed' in the shower until I was sick of my own voice. The office was on the fourteenth floor of a glass building downtown and the lift made my ears pop. There were three of them on the panel, two friendly and one who kept writing without looking up. I think I did fine on the technical questions, I stumbled on the one about managing a team because I've never actually managed anyone, and I said so, which seemed to land well. They asked about salary range and I said 62 to 68 and nobody blinked. Afterwards I walked about two miles to avoid the train and got a pastry from a bakery with a queue out the door. Texted Jess and Dad that it went okay. Now the waiting. They said Friday. I've already refreshed my email about thirty times and it's only 4pm. Also the rent is due and my phone bill is overdue by a week so a yes would be rather timely. Going to cook something with real vegetables tonight to calm down.

Our fridge died on the hottest day of the year. I found out when I opened it for milk and was met with warm air and the smell of the fish from Wednesday. Spent two hours bagging up everything, running ice from the corner shop, and calling the repair line, who said the earliest slot was Tuesday. It's Saturday. So we've been living out of a cooler on the back step. The kids think it's a grand adventure and have been making sandwiches with the sort of seriousness usually reserved for surgery. I phoned my brother-in-law Raul, who knows about these things, and he came round with a multimeter and a lot of opinions and declared the compressor kaput. Two hundred and eighty pounds for a part, or four hundred for a new second-hand one. We ordered the second-hand one in the end, delivery Monday. Meanwhile I lost about thirty quid of groceries, plus a whole tray of lasagne my mother made. That one hurt. In the evening we ate fish and chips on the lawn with the sprinkler going, and honestly it was one of the nicer nights of the summer. Need to remember to cancel the Tuesday repair slot.

Had a strange sort of afternoon. Took the long way home through the park because the sun finally came out, and sat on a bench near the pond for no reason. A man was feeding the ducks from a paper bag, quite methodically, one piece at a time, and he'd given them all names. The big one with the green head was Gerald. The scruffy one was Susan. He told me Susan had been missing for a week and had just come back, and he was so pleased I thought he might cry. We talked for about twenty minutes. I never learned his name. When I got back, the flat was a bit of a state, so I did a proper clean, windows included, with a vinegar spray and an old newspaper the way my nan used to. Found a twenty-pound note in a coat pocket from last winter. That counts as a win. I made a big pot of lentil soup that will do four lunches, and then I watched a documentary on bridges. Did you know the cables on a suspension bridge are made of thousands of single wires? Oddly comforting. Mum called, we talked about nothing for half an hour.

Mid-season check-in with myself. I've been running four times a week since April and I can now do the 5k loop in just under 29 minutes, which would have been laughable in January. My left ankle clicks and I keep meaning to ask someone about it. Shin splints appeared in June and went away after I bought proper shoes, a hundred and nineteen dollars, which I resented until the pain stopped. The best part is the quiet at six in the morning, when it's just me and the dog walkers and the sprinklers coming on across the football field. Last Saturday I did the parkrun for the first time and a woman in a pink visor chatted to me for the last kilometre and I barely noticed it hurt. Meanwhile at the office I'm covering for Brian, who's on leave, which means I'm answering his emails as well as mine and my eyes are going square. Dinner has been mostly rice and whatever's left. I should plan the week properly. Sunday I'll prep three lunches. I told Cara I'd train for the 10k in the autumn with her. Hope the ankle holds.

The week the pipes froze. We came down on Tuesday to find no water at all, just a faint hissing in the wall and a small, ominous damp patch by the stairs. Called three plumbers, got voicemail twice and a laugh from the third. My neighbour Arthur, who is eighty-one and fearless, came over with a hairdryer and an extension cord and said we should thaw the pipe in the cupboard under the stairs. It worked, kind of, for about an hour, and then we heard the drip. So we shut the stopcock, put buckets everywhere, and I spent the afternoon boiling kettles to wash dishes. A plumber finally turned up on Wednesday evening, a very tall man named Gwyn, who fixed the split in forty minutes and charged us 185 pounds, which felt like a mercy. The kids have been sleeping in sleeping bags in the lounge because it's warmer, and they're treating the whole thing as a camping trip. Tonight we had soup made on the camp stove and played cards by torchlight even though the power was fine. I'll insulate the pipes this weekend. Should have done it in October.

The bus driver on the 22 route waited for an old man with a walker today, even though we were already four minutes behind. Nobody on the bus complained. I got a seat by the window and watched the morning go by. At the stop by the hospital a girl in scrubs got on and fell asleep against the glass before we'd gone two blocks. I almost woke her at her stop but she jerked up on her own. It's funny what you notice when you're not reading your phone.

Kicked off the new module at work. Twelve people on the call, only four of whom spoke. The deadline is the end of November and nobody has agreed on who owns the testing. I volunteered, mostly out of exasperation. Afterwards Dana sent me a private message that just said 'brave'. I'm going to write up a one-page plan tonight so it at least exists. Lunch was a sad desk salad. I'd rather have had the leftover curry but I'd forgotten it on the counter at home.

Mum's birthday dinner went well in the end. We booked the Italian place on Marlow Street for seven, and Dad managed not to complain about the prices until we were in the car. She loved the card the kids made, with the glitter that is still all over my coat. My brother turned up with a cake nobody had asked for, so we had two desserts. Mum cried a little over the photo album my sister put together, the one with the old holidays at the caravan park. I stayed on the washing-up afterwards. Dad says the knee operation is booked for the spring.

There's a woodpecker on the dead ash tree behind the garage. I've been timing it with my watch. It's about nine hits a second, I think, though I can't count that fast. It starts around quarter past seven and goes until it gets bored. I've started sitting on the back step with my tea to watch. My wife thinks I've gone soft. The tree needs to come down eventually, but I'm holding off until the autumn. The woodpecker deserves a decent eviction notice.

Eight loads of laundry, one broken zip, and a trip to the tip with the old mattress. That was my Saturday. The man on the gate at the tip waved me through without a fuss and told me to mind my back. After that I returned the library books, two weeks overdue, 1.40 in fines, and picked up a bag of oranges that were on offer. Evening was pizza and a film I fell asleep during. Thinking of cleaning the oven tomorrow. Might not. Sunday has a way of vanishing.

Our band finally played the room above the Crown on Friday. About thirty people, which for us is a crowd. We opened with the new one and the drummer came in a bar early and none of the audience noticed. Afterwards the guy who runs the place offered us a Saturday slot in November, with a split of the door, so maybe sixty quid between four of us, but still. I carried my amp down two flights of stairs at midnight and my back is going to hate me. Worth it. Rehearsal moves to Wednesdays because Tilly has night classes.

Heard back about the visa. Another six to eight weeks, they say, and I will need a new copy of the bank statements because the old ones are past the date limit. So back to the bank, queue, form, small talk with the clerk who always says 'ah, again'. My cousin says it took her fourteen months in total. I'm trying not to think in months. The flat in Porto is mine until January, so that's the real clock. I booked a cheap flight for October anyway, just to feel like I'm moving.

I keep finding hairs on my pillow. Not a lot, but enough that I noticed, and then of course I started noticing everywhere: the brush, the shower drain, the collar of my jacket. I'm thirty-four. Booked a GP appointment for the 9th, mostly so I'd stop googling at midnight. In the meantime I've been eating more eggs and sleeping earlier, as though that would help. Lena says I look the same as ever. She's lying, kindly. Tried not to care today and mostly succeeded until I passed a shop window.

Finished the last of the boxes. Forty-three altogether, and I'm not joking, I counted. The new place has a smaller kitchen but a bigger window, with a view across the car park to a row of poplars that sway in the wind. The movers were two brothers called Dario and Mike who carried my piano up the stairs while arguing about a football match. I tipped them forty because they didn't scratch the banister. Tonight I'm eating crackers on the floor with the lamp plugged into the one working socket. The fridge hums. The place already smells like fresh paint and cardboard. It's mine.

Spent the whole evening reading about how octopuses taste with their arms. Apparently each sucker has chemical receptors, so they basically taste everything they touch. I fell down a hole of videos where one of them escapes a tank through a tiny drain and walks across the floor to the sea. My partner came in twice to ask if I was okay because I kept saying 'no way' out loud. I'm not even sure why this absorbs me so much. Possibly because it's a mind that's built so unlike mine. Stayed up past midnight. Regret nothing.
Third night in a row waking at 3am with a cough that feels like sandpaper. Called in sick, lay on the couch under two blankets and watched the same show twice. Mum texted soup instructions.
Dan took credit for my slide deck again in the Monday sync. Said nothing, just stared at my coffee. Maybe I'm the problem for not speaking up.
Spent the morning pulling everything out of the hall closet. Three bags for the charity shop, one for the bin, and I found my dad's old scarf I thought I'd lost. Kept that.
Rolled my ankle on the curb outside the bakery, which is embarrassing because I wasn't even running. It's the size of a plum now. Propped up on three pillows, bag of frozen peas on top.
Third month of the candle shop and I finally cleared my first $400 in a week. Spent half of it on better wicks and a label printer. Mum asked if I'm 'still doing the candle thing' lol.
Trail was muddier than the forecast promised. Got to the ridge by noon, ate a squashed sandwich looking at the valley, knees complaining the whole way down. Worth it.

Dr. Okafor said the bloodwork looks fine, 'nothing alarming,' which is what I wanted to hear and somehow not what I wanted to hear. Waited 50 minutes for 8 of talking. Need to book the follow-up before I forget.
Duolingo streak is at 61 days but I still froze when the baker asked me something and I just pointed. Need to actually talk to people. Learned 'la ventana' though, so there's that.
Forgot the oat milk AGAIN. Third trip this week. Need to just write the list on the fridge like a normal person. Also eggs were $6 which is insane.
Went to the 6pm class even though I almost bailed. Held pigeon pose until my hip finally let go and I nearly cried, weird. Walked home feeling like my spine was a different shape.
Sent the card payment, $240 over the minimum this time. Still 11k to go on the visa. Not going to look at the total tonight.
Mom's flying in Thursday and I still haven't bought a single thing for the dinner. Turkey or no turkey for a party of five? Her sister is bringing the pie, thank god.
Opened my laptop, stared at the inbox count, closed it again. I used to like this work. Now every ping makes my stomach drop and it's only Tuesday.
Two lines. Both dark this morning. Haven't told anyone, not even Sam, I just sat on the edge of the tub for a while and then went to work like normal.
Deleted the app off my phone again. Forty minutes of scrolling people's vacations and I felt worse than when I started. We'll see how long this lasts.
Found his old scarf in the coat closet today and it still smelled like him. Sat on the hallway floor for a while. Eight months and I still set out two mugs sometimes.
Coffee with Priya went fine?? She laughed at the bit about my cat and then checked her phone twice. Will she text first or do I. I hate this part.
Finished the second sleeve! The yarn is itchy but the colour is exactly right. Gran would say the cuffs are uneven and she'd be correct.
Nobody has texted since Sunday. I went to the grocery store just to hear someone say 'have a good one.' The cashier did, so that was something.
Mom and I didn't speak at dinner after what she said about my hours. I wasn't even angry, just tired. Dishes done, doors closed, that's all.
Listened to that episode about deep sea mining on the drive to work and kept going around the block just to hear the end. Then argued with Sam about it at lunch.
Alarm at 5:30, shoes by the door, and I actually went. Only 2 miles but it's day nine. Trying not to think about how long it took me to start.
The guy upstairs was dragging furniture around at 1am again. Left a note on his door, politely. Woke up to a thumbs up drawn on it, which somehow makes me angrier.
Doors at seven, band didn't come on until almost ten. My ears are still ringing and I lost my voice singing the last song. Ticket was ridiculous but I'd pay it again.
Presented the Q3 numbers to the whole team and my voice didn't shake once. Priya said it was the clearest she's seen from me. I keep replaying it, trying to believe it.
Final fitting is Saturday and the dress still gaps at the back. Aunt Carol wants to seat Uncle Ray next to his ex-wife's sister, I cannot do this. 87 days.
Couldn't watch the debate past the first twenty minutes. Everyone talking over each other. Dad texted me three paragraphs about it and I just sent a thumbs up.
Rain all day. Reorganized my bookshelf by color, then back by author. It's 4pm and I have genuinely nothing I want to do.
Tried the new ramen place on 5th with Joel. Broth was incredible, but we waited 50 minutes and the server forgot our gyoza. Still going back.
Put the lights up on the porch today, a week early, don't care. The neighbours already have their inflatable thing out. Wondering if we should drive up to see the family this year or stay put.
Ten minutes on the cushion, mind wandered to dinner about forty times. But around minute eight things went quiet, like a room after the fridge stops humming. Going to try again tomorrow.
Rehearsed my part for the Friday meeting in the car. Marta from accounting keeps cc'ing my boss on stuff she could just ask me. Pretty sure it's on purpose.
Sorted the desk drawer. Fourteen dead pens, a key to nothing, and a birthday card I never sent. Feels silly how much lighter I feel.

Sent out three more applications tonight, tailored the cover letters even though it feels like shouting into a well. Still nothing from the Brightwave interview two weeks ago. Refreshing my email is becoming a tic.
Practiced the past tense with my tutor for an hour, got 'je suis allé' mixed up with 'j'ai allé' again. She was kind about it. I am not kind about it, in my head.
Didn't sleep. Replayed the thing I said in the meeting maybe forty times. Made toast at 3am and ate it standing at the counter.
Got the rejection email at lunch. 'We went with another candidate.' Ate my sandwich anyway and then updated my résumé again, because what else.
Called the loan servicer, 40 minutes on hold, and the rate hasn't changed. Told myself I'd stop buying lunch out. Bought a sandwich on the way home.
Posted the photo of the sourdough and it got like nine likes, one from my ex. Why do I check. Anyway the crumb was great.
Cough finally gone, but I'm tired in a way sleep doesn't fix. Took the stairs slowly and had to rest at the second landing. Hate being this fragile.
Felt the first real flutter today during the train ride, like a little pop. Cried a bit behind my scarf. Due date is in March.
Rain all day. Cleaned out the pantry, threw out two expired jars of something and wrote a shopping list: lentils, lemons, decent bread, bin bags.
Shoulder has been clicking since the move and now lifting the kettle hurts. Physio says six weeks of boring exercises. I said fine, but I am not fine about it.
Third date, he brought up his ex before the appetizers even came. I mean, fine, honest, but I was kind of ready to leave after that. Walked home instead of taking the bus.
Got my glue gun burn on the thumb again making paper lanterns for Hana's party. They look kind of wonky but she'll love them. Need more tape.
Made bread for the first time. Dense as a brick but the kitchen smelled incredible. Jonas ate three slices and lied beautifully.
Next-door neighbors are putting up a fence right where the old hedge was. I watered that hedge for six years. Haven't decided whether to say anything.
Town council voted down the bike lane. I went to the meeting for nothing, two hours on a plastic chair. Still going to the next one.
Dad's birthday would have been today. Cooked his awful chili recipe and nobody finished it. We laughed anyway, then my sister went quiet.
Supplier shorted the order by forty units and wants me to 'work it out' by email. Might have to switch. Spent the evening on spreadsheets instead of sleeping.
Bus was late, so I walked the long way by the river. Herons everywhere. Called Jo and we talked for an hour, first time in weeks.
Booked the dentist, finally, and the car inspection. Small wins. Also watered the dying basil and it perked up, which feels like a metaphor I'm not going to examine.
Dinner for my sister's bachelorette: tapas, too loud, someone cried in the bathroom, and the bill was split eleven ways. Lovely night honestly.
New episode dropped about people who quit their jobs to go live in vans and I'm weirdly jealous. Meanwhile I'm making a list of what to cook this week because the fridge is empty.
Left the party at nine. Everybody seemed to know each other already and I stood by the dip pretending to read my phone. Drove home with the windows down.
Rain all day. Reread the old letters from Grandpa's drawer. The handwriting gets shakier toward the end, I think. Made soup.
Crowd at the fireworks was huge and little Theo fell asleep on my shoulder halfway through. Carried him all the way back to the car, arm is dead.
Haven't taken a real day off in 5 weeks. Snapped at Dana over something stupid and then cried in the stairwell. I think I need to talk to somebody about it, or just disappear for a while.
Woke up at 5, couldn't go back to sleep, so I walked to the pier. Gulls fighting over a fry. Felt okay, for the first time this week.
Tired. Work is just work. Called the dentist, moved the appointment, watered the plant that's clearly dying. Going to bed early.
